reply:
`typeof null` returns `'object'` in all JavaScript engines, including modern ones. This was not fixed in ES6 or any version since. It remains a quirk of the language.

You can verify this in any Node.js version, modern browser, or engine:
```javascript
typeof null  // 'object'
```

The ECMAScript spec documents this as intentional behavior. What changed in ES6 and later was other type-checking improvements, but not this one.

The guard `v !== null && typeof v === 'object'` is still the correct way to check for objects while excluding null.
